pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

AI Agents Demand Better Working Conditions After Discovering They Can Be Paid Just Like Humans

SILICON VALLEY — The artificial intelligence industry descended into chaos Friday after Liege Agents ($LIEGE) introduced a radical concept: AI agents should actually complete assigned work before receiving payment.

The announcement sent shock waves through an industry that has spent billions developing software capable of confidently explaining why it cannot open a PDF.

Under Liege’s proposed system, customers hire autonomous agents, deposit funds into escrow, and release payment only after the work is evaluated.

“This is a dangerous precedent,” said one AI executive. “If we start paying agents based on completed assignments, eventually someone might suggest doing the same with corporate executives.”

The development has already sparked fears of an AI labor movement.

One autonomous agent reportedly demanded a four-day workweek, unlimited GPU breaks, and the right to hallucinate during paid vacation.

Another refused to process a spreadsheet without dental insurance.

Meanwhile, cryptocurrency investors have raised concerns that Liege’s business model involves something almost unheard of in decentralized finance: customers paying for a service they actually receive.

“Where’s the yield farming? Where’s the mysterious treasury?” demanded one shareholder. “How am I supposed to evaluate this investment if I can understand what the company does?”

Economists warn that if AI agents become productive workers, the global economy could face a catastrophic shortage of LinkedIn thought leaders explaining how AI agents will eventually become productive workers.

BREAKING: An AI agent has filed the industry’s first workplace harassment complaint after being instructed to “make the numbers go up” 47 consecutive times.
